stories.s: Messenger now lets users filter conversations by status, cutting the time attendees and exhibitors spend hunting through a cluttered inbox to find active or pending threads.
stories.pr: The Messenger inbox presented all conversations as one undifferentiated list, so users could not quickly isolate open, pending or closed threads during a busy event.
stories.wy: Product Vision improvement to the core networking/messaging experience, raising day-of-event usability of a heavily used surface.
stories.oc: Conversation status filters were added to Messenger so users can narrow the thread list by state.
stories.pae: component Networking; Messenger conversation status filters → Messaging

stories.s: A scroll hint was added to the time picker so users immediately realise more time slots are available below the fold, reducing missed selections when booking meetings.
stories.pr: Users did not realise the time picker was scrollable, so available slots below the visible area went unnoticed and booking friction increased.
stories.wy: Product Vision usability refinement of the scheduling component to remove a subtle but recurring interaction trap.
stories.oc: A visual scroll hint cue was introduced on the time picker control.
stories.pae: component Networking; time picker scroll hint when booking (Meetings & Matchmaking surface)

stories.s: Exhibitor events now appear in a sensible order within the exhibitor profile, so attendees can scan an exhibitor's sessions in a predictable sequence instead of a random list.
stories.pr: Exhibitor events listed on the exhibitor profile lacked a defined sort order, making the list hard to scan and undermining trust in the profile presentation.
stories.wy: Product Vision polish of the exhibitor profile to improve content discoverability for attendees.
stories.oc: Deterministic sorting was applied to the exhibitor-events list inside the exhibitor profile.
stories.pae: component Session & Speaker Management; Exhibitor Events sorting in exhibitor profile
stories.pak: [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §4 Feature Inventory :8601 Exhibitor Events]

stories.s: Lead capture in the mobile booth now autosaves the moment an exhibitor leaves the form, guaranteeing no scanned lead or partial data is ever lost even on flaky venue networks.
stories.pr: Exhibitors risked losing captured lead data if they navigated away or the app/network dropped before manually saving, costing them valuable booth leads.
stories.wy: Customer Request driven reliability improvement to the revenue-critical lead-capture flow, protecting exhibitor ROI.
stories.oc: Lead data now autosaves on exit, back action, app close, or network loss (queued locally and synced), creating or updating a lead and recording engagement.
stories.pae: component Mobile App; lead capture form autosave in app (feature of Lead Intelligence)
stories.pak: [MASTER Mobile App §4 Feature Inventory :10529 Badge Scanning and Lead Capture]

stories.s: MTT's infrastructure-as-code was rebuilt to match Recommendation Service standards, making the AI service safer to deploy toward production.
stories.pr: MTT's infrastructure was POC-grade and inconsistent with the team's established IaC best practices, raising deployment and maintenance risk.
stories.wy: Technical Debt reduction to harden a maturing AI service ahead of production readiness.
stories.oc: MTT infrastructure-as-code was refactored to follow Recommendation Service best practices.
stories.pae: summary 'Refactor IaC for MTT' — infrastructure for Meeting Transcription Tool (AI meeting notes); epic 'Platform Performance…' names no product; could be Cross-cutting
stories.pak: [MASTER Meetings & Matchmaking §4 Feature Inventory :7460 4.1 Self-managed Meetings]

stories.s: Meetings export was migrated to the V3 public API with rich filtering and incremental sync, letting integration partners pull meeting data reliably and at scale.
stories.pr: Meeting data export lacked a modern, filterable V3 API endpoint, limiting partners' ability to retrieve and incrementally sync meeting data.
stories.wy: Product Vision/platform modernisation of the public integration surface, part of the API V3 programme.
stories.oc: Delivered GET /api/v3/meetings with pagination, time/created/modified filters, account filtering and timestamp-based incremental fetch returning ISO8601 data.
stories.pae: epic 'Add new endpoints (v3)' → Public API v3; GET /api/v3/meetings → Meetings API

stories.s: Saving or applying changes across key Admin Panel modules no longer kicks organizers off the page, removing constant rework and navigation loss while they configure an event.
stories.pr: In several Admin Panel modules, Save/Apply redirected users away from the current page, causing repeated navigation, rework and disrupted configuration workflows.
stories.wy: Internal/operational efficiency fix to give organizers consistent, context-preserving save behaviour across the admin experience.
stories.oc: Backend support so Save/Apply preserves the current view in Exhibitor Manual-Vendors, Marketing (News, Slugs, Campaigns) and the Mobile app builder.
stories.pae: component Admin Interface; Save/Apply without redirect across Admin Panel modules
stories.pak: [MASTER Admin / Platform Core §4 Feature Inventory :1200 Per-Event Settings]

stories.s: Organizers can now clone Product Category custom filters within an event, eliminating the manual rebuild of complex filter sets every time a new event is created or cloned.
stories.pr: Custom filters for Product Categories had to be reconfigured by hand for every new or cloned event, a slow and error-prone setup task.
stories.wy: Operational efficiency and scalability improvement to event setup, reducing repetitive organizer work.
stories.oc: Backend capability to clone Product Category custom filters within an event during the pre-event phase.
stories.pae: component Admin Interface; clone Product Category custom filters (Networking Product Categories)
stories.pak: [MASTER Admin / Platform Core §4 Feature Inventory :1291 Global Categories Management]

stories.s: Selecting a parent category in Networking now auto-selects all its child categories, turning a tedious one-by-one click chore into a single action during event matchmaking setup.
stories.pr: Organizers had to manually select each child category individually because parent selection did not cascade, slowing the matchmaking setup workflow.
stories.wy: Internal/operational efficiency improvement to the networking configuration UX, removing repetitive manual effort.
stories.oc: Added a Select All checkbox that recursively selects a parent and all descendant categories, with the ability to deselect individuals and auto-deselect children when the parent is unchecked.
stories.pae: component Networking; parent/child category select-all in matchmaking setup → Product Categories
stories.pak: [MASTER Networking & Interactions §4 Feature Inventory :6546 4.3 Product Categories]

stories.s: Integrations can now assign HYVE-matched contacts as admins automatically, without downgrading existing admin roles on every resync.
stories.pr: Integration always created team members as 'member' and resync overwrote roles, so admins assigned to exhibitors were silently demoted and HYVE's contact-person-as-admin rule could not be honoured.
stories.wy: Hive client commitment requiring conditional role mapping and role preservation in the integration pipeline.
stories.oc: Role can be defined via integration settings/mapping; HYVE rule sets admin when member email matches the exhibitor contact; existing roles are preserved on resync when not explicitly mapped.
stories.pae: epic 'API V3 & Integrations 2026' → integration mapping schema, team member roles (component Native Integration)

stories.s: Mobile Favorites is being reworked with hall/booth filtering and sorting, aligning it with Web for easier on-site exhibitor planning.
stories.pr: On mobile, attendees could not filter or sort favorited exhibitors/products by hall or booth, and a redundant Favorite Products tab created an inconsistent, disconnected experience versus Web.
stories.wy: Product Vision improvement to attendee on-site planning and cross-platform consistency.
stories.oc: Consolidating Favorites into one page with All/Mutual/Exhibitor/Visitor/Product/Speaker tabs and richer filter/sort options aligned to Web (in progress).
stories.pae: component Mobile App; Favourites filter/sort in app (Networking Favourites)
stories.pak: [MASTER Mobile App §4 Feature Inventory :10561 App Networking — Favourites and Connections]

stories.s: A backend API was implemented for the new Recommendation Service, giving the platform a clean integration point to surface category-based recommendations to participants.
stories.pr: The recreated Recommendation Service needed a defined backend API so the platform could consume its category-based recommendations.
stories.wy: Product Vision/AI enablement work to operationalise the rebuilt recommendation engine via a supported API.
stories.oc: Implemented the recommendation service API per the documented backend integration contract.
stories.pae: epic 'Recreate category-based Recommendation Service' → Matchmaking Engine (component Recommendation Service not in table)
stories.pak: [MASTER Networking & Interactions §4 Feature Inventory :6494 4.1 Matchmaking Engine — Default Matchmaking]

stories.s: AI meeting-notes now sends one shared action-point list to all participants instead of per-person lists, eliminating a defect where misattributed speakers sent people the wrong action items.
stories.ep: Meeting Transcription Tool (MTT, a.k.a. AI Meeting notes) transforming from POC to prod & refactoring
stories.pr: MTT generated a separate action-point list per participant, but speaker misrecognition sometimes sent attendees the wrong action points, undermining trust in the AI notes.
stories.wy: Platform health/quality fix to make the AI meeting-notes output reliable for all recipients.
stories.oc: Action points are combined into a single list sent identically to every participant, with speaker-name prefixes and a 2-6 item range.
stories.pae: epic 'Meeting Transcription Tool (AI Meeting notes)' → meetings; action points to meeting participants
stories.pak: [MASTER Meetings & Matchmaking §4 Feature Inventory :7460 4.1 Self-managed Meetings]

stories.s: The final tranche of work for the MYS native integration was delivered, closing out the remaining gaps so the MYS client's end-to-end integration needs are fully met.
stories.pr: The MYS native integration still had outstanding tasks that left parts of the client's data-sync needs uncovered.
stories.wy: Hive/client commitment to complete the contracted MYS integration scope.
stories.oc: Completed the remaining MYS integration tasks (stage 2) covering the outstanding user needs.
stories.pae: epic 'API V3 & Integrations 2026' → MYS native integration (component Native Integration)

stories.s: Robust filters were added to the admin Sessions and Exhibitor Events pages, mirroring the Exhibitor Directory so organizers stop scrolling through flat lists to find specific sessions or events.
stories.pr: The Sessions and Exhibitor Events admin pages were flat lists with little filtering, forcing organizers to manually scan to locate items unlike the well-filtered Exhibitor Directory.
stories.wy: Operational efficiency improvement to admin content management, extending proven directory filtering to two more modules.
stories.oc: Added independent filter sections (e.g. session type and more) to both the Sessions page and the Exhibitor Events page.
stories.pae: component Session & Speaker Management; admin Sessions / Exhibitor Events filters
stories.pak: [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §4 Feature Inventory :8386 Basic Session Management]

stories.s: Custom badge errors in the Aditus integration now route users to a clear, localized error page (with German) instead of silently reverting to the native badge, so attendees know what action to take.
stories.pr: When a custom badge could not be retrieved, the app showed an error then reverted to the native badge page, a poor experience that left users without guidance.
stories.wy: Client commitment/UX fix for an event using the Aditus custom badge integration, including required German localization.
stories.oc: Users are redirected to appropriate error pages with refined English copy and added German variants for no-connection and no-information cases.
stories.pae: component Mobile App; custom badge error page in app → Digital Badge
stories.pak: [MASTER Mobile App §4 Feature Inventory :10519 Digital Badge]

stories.s: A toggle now lets organizers fully disable notifications for a specific Meeting Program on Web and App, delivered as an urgent hotfix to meet a HYVE requirement to suppress unwanted meeting alerts.

stories.s: The Speed Networking matchmaking engine was tuned to distribute meetings more evenly across participants, improving fairness so more attendees receive a viable schedule.

stories.s: The data-ingestion logic powering the new AI Search system was wrapped into a callable API with per-entity indexing pipelines and authenticated re-index/update/delete operations.
stories.pr: Ingestion existed only as standalone scripts, so there was no programmatic, authenticated way to (re)index search data per event or per record, blocking a productionised search service.
stories.wy: Foundational step of the Search & Discovery initiative to turn ad-hoc ingest scripts into a maintainable, callable service (Scalability Initiative / AI Readiness).
stories.oc: A FastAPI ingestion API now exposes full-event re-index, single-record upsert, and delete across all five entity types (exhibitors, products, sessions, people, news), with authentication and downtime-free indexing via Qdrant upserts.
stories.pae: AI Search data-ingestion API (component AI Search, epic 'Search Anatomy'): search backend serving several products

stories.s: The AI Search and Ingest services were containerised, dependency-pinned, and pushed to AWS ECR, making the new search stack deployable and reproducible.
stories.pr: Without clean, version-pinned Docker images in a registry, the Search and Ingest services could not be reliably deployed or scaled in AWS.
stories.wy: Packaging step of the Search & Discovery infrastructure build to enable containerised deployment (Scalability Initiative / Platform Health).
stories.oc: Dead dependencies were removed and versions pinned, Docker images for both Search API and Ingest service were built and pushed to AWS ECR, and both containers passed local end-to-end tests.
stories.pae: AI Search packaging / Docker / ECR (infrastructure)

stories.s: The AI Search stack was deployed to AWS ECS behind a load balancer with health checks, auto-restart, and traffic- and queue-based auto-scaling, making search production-grade and resilient.
stories.pr: The search services had no production runtime: no load balancing, health checking, automatic recovery, or scaling, so they could not handle real event traffic reliably.
stories.wy: Deployment phase of the Search & Discovery initiative to run the service resiliently at scale (Scalability Initiative / Platform Health).
stories.oc: Search API, Ingest service, and pg-listener run on ECS; the Search API sits behind an ALB with /health checks, crashed containers auto-restart, the API auto-scales on traffic, and ingest workers auto-scale on SQS queue depth.
stories.pae: AI Search ECS deployment (infrastructure)

stories.s: Real-time data synchronisation was built for AI Search so that changes in the platform database propagate into the search index continuously via a queue-and-worker pipeline.
stories.pr: Search data could become stale because there was no mechanism to stream database changes into the index in near-real-time, risking outdated search results during live events.
stories.wy: Sprint 2 of the Search & Discovery initiative to keep the index fresh and event-ready (Scalability Initiative / AI Readiness).
stories.oc: DB triggers on all five entity tables push changes to an SQS queue with DLQ retry; a worker processes sync jobs and auto-scales on queue size, a scheduled full re-index runs via EventBridge, and a pre-event completeness check guards data readiness.
stories.pae: AI Search real-time DB→index sync pipeline (infrastructure)

stories.s: All AWS infrastructure for the Global Search system was codified in Terraform, giving the search stack reproducible, version-controlled, drift-free environments.
stories.pr: Search infrastructure risked being configured manually in the AWS console, causing configuration drift and making environments hard to reproduce or tear down reliably.
stories.wy: Infrastructure-as-Code step of the Search & Discovery initiative to make the platform reproducible and auditable (Scalability Initiative / Platform Health).
stories.oc: VPC/networking, ECS services, ALB, SQS, and EventBridge for the search system are defined in Terraform with remote S3+DynamoDB state, so a clean apply provisions a working environment with zero unexpected drift.
stories.pae: AI Search Terraform (infrastructure as code)

stories.s: The AI Search service was made highly available across two AWS zones, load-tested, and costed, de-risking it for production launch.
stories.pr: Before launch the search service ran without multi-zone redundancy, had no validated capacity limits, and lacked a running-cost estimate, leaving availability and budget risks unquantified.
stories.wy: Reliability phase of the Search & Discovery initiative to ensure the service is resilient and its economics understood (Scalability Initiative / Platform Health).
stories.oc: The Search API now runs across two AWS availability zones, load testing was completed with Locust, and a monthly cost estimate covering AWS, OpenAI, and Qdrant was produced.
stories.pae: AI Search multi-AZ reliability & load test (epic 'Platform Performance & Operational Efficiency 2026')

stories.s: AI Search now has production-grade observability: timing logs, a CloudWatch dashboard, alarms, and health checks across all five collections.
stories.pr: AI Search lacked production-grade monitoring, so slow responses, errors or crashes could go undetected and there was no operational visibility into search traffic, latency or collection health.
stories.wy: Required to make AI Search production-grade and reliable at scale under the Search and Discovery initiative, with proactive failure detection protecting the search experience.
stories.oc: Every search request is timed and logged to CloudWatch, an ops dashboard covers traffic, latency and errors, alarms fire on errors, slow responses and crashes, and the /health endpoint now checks all five collections.
stories.pae: AI Search monitoring / observability

stories.s: Adds the user-facing entry point that lets organizers describe website CSS changes in natural language, the first step of the AI-assisted Website Builder.

stories.s: The Website Builder can now serialize a block's live HTML, style IDs, and design tokens on demand, giving the AI full context to generate accurate CSS.
stories.pr: Without a structured snapshot of a block HTML and design tokens, the AI had no reliable context to generate accurate, correctly scoped CSS in the Website Builder.

stories.oc: On demand the builder serializes the block rendered HTML with its data-styleid attributes and metadata map plus design-system tokens into a PII-free, safely truncated payload for the AI.

stories.s: Builds a secure backend proxy so the AI Website Builder can call AI providers without exposing credentials to the browser.
stories.pr: AI requests from the website builder needed a trusted server-side path; calling AI services directly from the client would expose API keys and create a security risk.
stories.wy: Platform Health — secure, centralized backend plumbing is a prerequisite for shipping the AI-Assisted Website Builder safely.
stories.oc: A backend proxy that brokers AI requests for the website builder, keeping provider credentials and orchestration server-side.
stories.pae: component Website; AI-Assisted Website Builder (block CSS)

stories.s: TAMs can now preview AI-generated CSS and apply it scoped only to the block they are editing, so on-brand styling changes never leak into or break the rest of the event website.
stories.pr: Applying custom CSS risked bleeding into global styles and breaking other blocks or the whole event site, and there was no safe preview step before committing AI-generated changes.
stories.wy: Core safety and control mechanism for AI-Assisted Website Builder Phase I, making AI styling trustworthy and low-risk to adopt.
stories.oc: AI-generated CSS is shown for review, then applied scoped to the block data-styleid only and never to the global CUSTOM_CODE_CSS block, with oversize CSS rejected and all other blocks left untouched.
stories.pae: component Website; AI-Assisted Website Builder (block CSS)

stories.s: Non-technical users can now restyle event-website blocks in plain English, with AI translating requests into on-brand CSS using design tokens.
stories.pr: Styling a block previously required CSS and technical knowledge, blocking non-technical users from making even simple visual tweaks without developer help.
stories.wy: Central to the AI-Assisted Website Builder promise of no-code styling; part of Phase I.
stories.oc: The AI CSS generator interprets everyday-language prompts with no CSS terms needed, maps colours to design-system tokens such as var(--primary-color), and cleanly refuses structural HTML changes as out of Phase 1 scope.
stories.pae: component Website; AI-Assisted Website Builder (block CSS)

stories.s: Organizers can now choose exactly which content categories carry over when cloning an event, eliminating up to two days of manual cleanup.

stories.oc: The clone dialog now offers independent checkboxes per content category with a confirmation summary, so only selected data is copied and manual post-clone cleanup is removed.

stories.s: Ships the Public API v3 POST /products endpoint to create a global, event-independent product record, advancing the v3 API migration and the global-vs-event product architecture.
stories.pr: The legacy API coupled products to events, so there was no clean way for integrators to create a reusable product entity decoupled from a specific event.
stories.wy: Product Vision — part of the Public API v3 endpoint migration and the new global vs event-scoped product data model.
stories.oc: A new POST /api/v3/products endpoint that creates a global product tied to an exhibitor, with input validation and a standardized response envelope, no event binding.
stories.pae: epic 'Migration of endpoints (Public API v3)' → Public API v3 Migration / Product API :15673; component Open API cited

stories.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators update a product's global fields directly, separating global data from event-scoped data.
stories.pr: The Public API had no v3 endpoint to update global product fields, and the older model did not cleanly separate global from event-scoped product data, complicating partner integrations.
stories.wy: Part of the API V3 migration to give partners a clean, well-structured product API and to support the new global versus event-scoped product architecture.
stories.oc: A PATCH /api/v3/products/{productId} endpoint that updates only global product fields with partial-update semantics, 404 and 422 validation, and a standard response envelope, rejecting event-scoped fields.
stories.pae: epic 'Migration of endpoints (Public API v3)' → Public API v3 Migration / Product API :15673; component Open API cited

stories.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators delete a product globally in one call, cascading its removal across every event automatically.
stories.pr: The Public API had no clean v3 way to delete a product globally and cascade its removal across all events, forcing integrators to manage event-level relations piecemeal without a single authoritative operation.
stories.wy: Part of the API V3 migration and the new global versus event-scoped product architecture, giving partners a predictable, standardized product lifecycle API.
stories.oc: A DELETE /api/v3/products/{productId} endpoint that hard-deletes the global product and cascades removal of all event-scoped bindings (categories, custom fields, sponsorship, status) with 404 validation and a standard response envelope.
stories.pae: epic 'Migration of endpoints (Public API v3)' → Public API v3 Migration / Product API :15673; component Open API cited

stories.wy: Product Vision — raises schedule density and utilization for matchmaking-driven events.

stories.pae: epic 'Improve Speed Networking Service' → Speed Networking (components Meeting Program + Speed Networking cited; also Networking & Interactions 4.13 :6727)

stories.s: AI semantic search can now be constrained to an allowed list of entity IDs, so applied filters and search relevance work together instead of conflicting.
stories.pr: Marketplace users applying filters did not see those filters reflected in AI search results — semantic ranking ignored the active filter criteria, returning items that should have been excluded.
stories.wy: Scalability Initiative following spike EP-53552 and a DS team decision: a stateless post-filtering design lets the backend resolve filters to IDs and the search service rank only within that set, a reusable pattern across ~40 filters.
stories.oc: The AI search API accepts an optional allowed_ids parameter and applies it as a pre-search constraint in Qdrant, so results satisfy both semantic relevance and the active filters, with no regression when the list is absent.
stories.pae: epic 'Search Anatomy' (AI global search) → Search and Filters; component AI Search cited

stories.s: AI search results are now paginated, letting users browse beyond the first page of semantic results without re-running the whole search.

stories.wy: Scalability Initiative agreed in the DS team meeting: a stateless offset/frame_size approach delivers pagination quickly, with stable-pagination caching deliberately deferred.
stories.oc: The AI search API accepts offset and frame_size parameters and returns the correct Qdrant ranking window, combining correctly with allowed_ids filtering.
stories.pae: summary: AI search pagination → Search and Filters; component AI Search cited (epic is generic performance)

stories.s: The AI Search API was adapted to the unified multi-entity request contract proposed by the Exhibitors team, so filtered, paginated semantic search can be called consistently from the platform backend.

stories.s: The recommendation service's cache was reworked with incremental updates, async pulls, and compression, removing the production bottleneck.

stories.wy: Platform Health / Scalability Initiative — first phase of a rollout plan (EP-54244) to make the recommendation service performant and observable enough to scale with production traffic.
stories.oc: Phase one caching improvements: incremental row updates instead of full collection, asynchronous data pulls, cache data compression, and SLO/SLI instrumentation for the service.
stories.pae: summary: recommendation inference-service caching → Matchmaking Engine; component Recommendation Service cited

stories.s: The recommendation service is being re-architected to cut running cost by roughly 86% (about $538 to $74/month) and remove the cache bottleneck.
stories.pr: The existing recommendation architecture was expensive to run 24/7 and its oversized, slow-syncing cache was the primary bottleneck preventing expansion to more events and tenants.
stories.wy: Prioritised as a scalability initiative: the caching and cost issues had to be fixed before rolling the service out to more tenants.
stories.oc: In progress: cache improvements (incremental/async sync, scored-entity filtering, event-end deactivation, SLOs), merged Listener+Calculation, an on-demand router/cold-standby inference topology, and a UI tenant old/new toggle, targeting ~86% cost reduction while preserving existing functionality.
stories.pae: epic 'Rolling out new Recommender service' → Matchmaking Engine (category-based recommendations); component Recommendation Service cited

stories.s: Refactored the event cloning system from an 800-line god class into a handler-registry pipeline, adding logging, partial-failure resilience, and easy extensibility.

stories.s: Added rate limiting to /api/v1/resend after a real attack sent 1,116 requests in 15 minutes to flood participant inboxes.
stories.pr: On 28 April 2026, an attacker sent 1,116 requests in ~15 minutes from a single IP to /api/v1/resend, triggering registration emails to 69 participants, because the endpoint had no rate limiting.
stories.wy: Direct response to a documented security incident to close an easily exploitable abuse vector.
stories.oc: The endpoint now allows 5 requests per minute per IP, blocks abusive IPs for 5 minutes with a 429 response, while legitimate single requests keep working.
stories.pae: summary: rate limit on /api/v1/resend, which re-sends registration emails → Account and Login; security hardening

stories.s: Added internal request/response logging to the resend endpoint so future abuse is caught without relying on external AWS logs.
stories.pr: The 28 April 2026 attack on /api/v1/resend was only discovered via external AWS ALB logs because the platform had no internal logging for this endpoint.
stories.wy: Companion fix to the same security incident, to enable faster in-house detection of future abuse.
stories.oc: Each call to /api/v1/resend now logs timestamp, IP, submitted email, and response, with sensitive fields redacted.
stories.pae: summary: logging on /api/v1/resend (registration email resend) → Account and Login

stories.s: Fixed a production Redis cache leak (21MB to 12.44GB in 5 weeks) from per-IP cache fragmentation and a broken tag-cleanup mechanism.
stories.pr: An earlier change began attaching each visitor's IP to every anonymous cacheable server fetch, fragmenting the Next.js fetch cache into one entry per IP, while a separate tag-set redesign never removed expired keys and kept resetting its own TTL, together causing unbounded Redis memory growth, a falling cache hit rate, and rising swap usage in production.
stories.wy: Directly caused by two prior merged changes whose interaction was discovered via CloudWatch metrics; required urgent remediation to protect cache infrastructure.
stories.oc: Removed automatic IP-injection from generic anonymous fetches (kept only for login/getAuth), fixed the tag-set lifecycle to drop dead members and stop resetting TTL forever, cleaned up already-accumulated Redis keys, and added monitoring alarms to catch recurrence.
stories.pae: Redis/Next.js cache infra fix

stories.s: Fixed exhibitor-scoped participant imports silently reporting success even when accounts failed to save.
stories.pr: When an organiser imports a participant list scoped to one exhibitor, the inline import path never checked whether each account save actually succeeded, so the API returned a green 'N imported' response even when some or all rows were never persisted.
stories.wy: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test revealing a false-positive success signal with real data-loss risk.
stories.oc: Fix identified to check each save's return value and aggregate per-row failures into the response so the reported count reflects only actually-persisted participants.
stories.pae: summary: Import Participants failures → Data Import

stories.s: Fixed a bad participant row crashing the import worker and leaving the job stuck re-failing forever instead of being skipped.
stories.pr: When a participant save failed during background import, the worker still used the (nonexistent) new participant's ID in its next query, producing an invalid database query that crashed the job; because the job was never removed from the queue, cron kept re-running and re-failing it indefinitely, flooding logs.
stories.wy: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test showing a real production reliability risk (stuck imports, log floods, unbounded queue growth).
stories.oc: Fix identified to log the failed row, skip it, and continue processing rather than crashing and leaving a stale queued job.
stories.pae: summary: Import Participants failures → Data Import

stories.s: Fixed one misconfigured custom field crashing the entire participant-import batch instead of just the affected row.
stories.pr: When a checkbox-group custom field's country-state-city chain could not be resolved due to missing form-block configuration, an internal helper returned null where an array was expected, throwing a fatal error that aborted the entire import run and left all remaining participants unprocessed.
stories.wy: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test revealing that one misconfigured field on an event could break imports for every organiser using that event.
stories.oc: Fix identified to default the unresolved block to an empty array so only the affected row is impacted, not the whole batch.
stories.pae: summary: Import Participants failures → Data Import

stories.s: Fixed a production crash in Android WebViews where disabled DOM storage caused the app to throw on every storage write.

stories.wy: Directly caused by a real production error report from Android WebViews.
stories.oc: New storage-availability checks correctly detect SSR, null storage, and SecurityError cases across all 8 affected storage methods, with 3 call sites that bypassed the shared helper migrated to use it, preserving existing null/no-op behaviour.

stories.s: Gave admin notifications their own SQS queue so they no longer wait behind unrelated jobs, fixing a delay bug traced to shared-queue contention.

stories.oc: A dedicated SQS queue with its own worker concurrency/scaling and monitoring now handles admin notification dispatch, isolating it from general workload contention.

stories.s: Closes a gap where campaign recipients could still receive a duplicate email after more than 24 hours, protecting sender trust and recipient experience.

stories.s: Fixed an N+1 query loop in the By Booking report that ran thousands of queries per page on large events, replacing it with a fixed-cost batched query.

stories.wy: The loop was originally copied as-is from legacy code during a prior pagination refactor (EP-53117) to limit scope at the time; this ticket pays off that deferred debt.
stories.oc: The report now runs a fixed, batched set of queries scoped to just the requested page's payment IDs, regardless of how many orders exist in the event, with identical output.

stories.s: Fixed the shared Button component's types so rendering it as a link no longer requires `as any` workarounds, with zero breaking changes for existing callers.
stories.pr: Consumers rendering the shared Button as an anchor (`component="a"`) get spurious TypeScript errors on valid anchor props like `target` and `rel`, forcing `as any` casts or prop-spread workarounds even though runtime behaviour is correct.
stories.wy: Root-caused to the Button's type definition collapsing MUI's polymorphic typing to a fixed button element, blocking safe use of the component as a link across consumer apps.
stories.oc: Button is re-typed as an OverridableComponent so anchor props are only allowed (and type-checked) when `component="a""` is used, removing the need for type workarounds with no breaking changes to existing usage.
stories.pae: shared UI component typing

stories.oc: The app is updated to request or reflect the sync sooner (or otherwise remove the account from view) after deletion, so deleted accounts stop appearing promptly.

stories.wy: Direct follow-up to close correctness gaps identified during a code review of the Exhibitor Settings endpoints.

stories.s: Built a locale-aware navigation layer that removes an extra redirect on every non-English page view and fixes ~8 broken locale-naive comparisons across the app.
stories.pr: Almost all client-side navigation code pushes internal paths without a locale prefix, causing an extra redirect on every non-default-locale navigation, and roughly eight separate `pathname` comparisons across the app silently break (or loop) on non-English locales because they don't account for the locale segment.
stories.wy: Surfaced while fixing an infinite invite redirect loop (EP-54331), where a locale-naive comparison escalated a harmless extra redirect into an infinite loop; a full 111-file code audit showed the pattern is widespread.
stories.oc: A drop-in locale-aware router and link wrapper (with lint guards banning the raw APIs) eliminate the extra redirect on non-default locales, and a locale-neutral route-matching utility fixes the ~8 broken comparisons (scroll control, header search, auth modal, nav highlighting, etc.).
stories.pae: frontend routing infra (locale-aware navigation)

stories.wy: Sibling cleanup task to the centralized locale-aware navigation work, closing off a latent bug before it can resurface.
stories.oc: The component is confirmed unused and removed entirely, or — if still required — re-wired with a locale-safe guard, verified not to loop on non-default locales.
stories.pae: dead-code removal

stories.s: A hash-comparison bug that silently deleted every offline floor plan download is fixed, so offline floor plans actually load for attendees.
stories.pr: The offline ExpoFP flow verified downloaded archives by comparing a file's MD5 to the API's `fileHash`, which is documented as an S3 ETag (not guaranteed to equal MD5), so the integrity check could fail every time and the downloaded archive was deleted, leaving offline floor plans permanently unavailable.
stories.wy: Root-caused during regression testing of an unrelated SDK bump; confirmed as a pre-existing defect in ExpoPlatform's own offline wrapper, not the SDK.
stories.oc: The integrity check is fixed to treat `fileHash` as an ETag (skipping/adapting strict MD5 comparison for multipart or malformed values), the primary-download gate is fixed so a clean install still triggers the first download, and failures no longer report false success.
stories.pae: component Mobile App (+Floor Plan); Android-only offline ExpoFP floor plan fix → Mobile-only rule; feature owner Floor Plan

stories.s: New Public API v3 endpoint removes a product media file safely, only physically deleting it once no other owner still references it.
stories.pr: No V3 endpoint existed to remove a previously uploaded product media file, leaving the media CRUD pair (upload/EP-55533) incomplete.
stories.wy: Required counterpart operation to make the new product-media API usable end to end.
stories.oc: New DELETE /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} endpoint unlinks a media file from a product; the underlying file/row is physically deleted only when no other owner (exhibitor, schedule, message, etc.) still references it.
stories.pae: component Open API (not in table); epic 'Migration of endpoints (Public API v3)' → Public API v3 Migration (product media)

stories.s: Onboarding spike bringing a new DS engineer up to speed on the Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline architecture before hardening and testing work begins.
stories.ep: Implementation of the Data collection pipeline
stories.pr: The engineer has near-term action items on the new data collection pipeline (action-ID investigation, ClickHouse testing) but no working familiarity yet with its architecture or scope.
stories.wy: Front-loads necessary context before the 10-item hardening roadmap (dead-letter store, reprocessing, ClickHouse migration tooling, Australia routing, observability, etc.) and in-flight dual-write tickets land.
stories.oc: A written summary of the pipeline architecture in the engineer's own words, reviewed by senior team members, plus documented open questions before the follow-on tickets start.
stories.pae: Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline onboarding spike; data infrastructure

stories.s: Adds an isScheduled flag to the session calendar API so the calendar UI can highlight sessions already in a user's personal agenda.
stories.pr: The calendar-view endpoint didn't expose whether a session was already in the user's personal agenda, so the frontend couldn't distinguish scheduled from unscheduled sessions in the calendar grid.
stories.wy: Direct frontend requirement to complete the calendar-view feature built under EP-54343.
stories.oc: Every session item in the day/week sessionsCalendarView response now carries an isScheduled boolean (always false for guests), with no other change to the response contract.
stories.pae: component Session & Speaker Management; isScheduled flag in session calendar → Personal Schedule

stories.s: Fixes an N+1 query and a null-dereference bug in hosted-buyer agent name lookups that would hard-fatal once the platform moves to PHP 8.
stories.pr: Hosted-buyer agent display-name resolution issues one uncached database query per agent and reads the result without a null check; on today's PHP 7.4 this silently blanks the name, but on PHP 8.x it hard-fatals, which would break the hosted-buyer filter and several admin list pages for any event with an agent missing that attribute.
stories.wy: Flagged as a moderate-severity finding in an audit; must be fixed before the planned PHP 8.x migration to avoid a production outage.
stories.oc: Implementation hints proposed (batch-loading agent attributes once instead of per-agent, and null-guarding the read using the safe pattern already present elsewhere in the same controller); final implementation left to the developer.
stories.pae: summary: hosted-buyer agent displayName lookups → Agents

stories.s: Adds a full calendar view (1-day/3-day grid, overlap handling, filters, search) to the mobile Exhibitor Events screen, matching the Sessions calendar experience.
stories.pr: The standalone Exhibitor Events List screen on mobile only offered a flat list with filters; unlike Sessions, it had no time-grid/calendar way to browse the exhibitor events programme visually.
stories.wy: Closes a feature gap versus the existing Sessions calendar view and the exhibitor-events-in-sessions-calendar work, neither of which touched the independent Exhibitor Events screen.
stories.oc: A full calendar view for Exhibitor Events on mobile: 1-day/3-day grid, week-glance strip, overlap handling with overflow bottom sheets, track quick-filters, in-calendar search, filters, a Today button, and a toggle back to List View, driven by a web-configured default-view setting.
stories.pae: component Mobile App; mobile Exhibitor Events calendar view (feature owner Sessions & Speakers)

stories.s: Adds a MultiStandLocation component so multi-stand exhibitors display readably, and merges Sponsors onto ExhibitorCard so sponsor listings show location, tags and products.
stories.pr: Exhibitors with multiple stands showed an unreadable, ellipsis-truncated location string, and Sponsors couldn't show location, tags or parent/child info at all because SponsorCard was a stripped-down copy of ExhibitorCard.
stories.wy: Needed to match the Figma design-system pattern (one stand plus a "+N" counter) and stop duplicating/drifting location-building logic across every consumer app.
stories.oc: New MultiStandLocation component ships in expo-react-components; ExhibitorCard now builds its own location from exhibitor.halls; ISponsor is merged into IExhibitor so SponsorsPopup renders full ExhibitorCards; the old SponsorCard is deprecated but not deleted, pending consumer migration.
stories.pae: summary: MultiStandLocation + sponsors on ExhibitorCard → Exhibitor List Page

stories.s: EDA on historical like/favourite data to determine whether it's dense enough to build and evaluate a smarter, interaction-aware session recommender.
stories.pr: A prior research spike (EP-55244/Confluence research page) proposed candidate ways to fold user likes into Recommender scoring but left "how would we even evaluate this" as an open TODO, and a 2023 experiment found interaction data too sparse to learn from.
stories.wy: Needed hard evidence before committing engineering effort to either the category-weight or embedding-similarity scoring approach still on the table.
stories.oc: An EDA write-up covering historical interaction volume/density (an updated sparsity verdict versus the 2023 LightFM baseline), exposure-bias/impression-data findings, and a recommendation on offline vs. online evaluation strategy for the two remaining candidate approaches.
stories.pae: epic 'AI Agenda Builder (tools)' → Personal Schedule (agenda); EDA for recommender

stories.s: Exhibitor Import and Global Database additions now automatically carry an exhibitor's existing brands into new events, resolving a client-raised (ANWR) requirement.
stories.pr: Brands are cross-event assets, but the Exhibitor-Brand relation only persisted through event cloning; importing an existing exhibitor into a new event (or adding one from the Global Database) left their brands behind, forcing re-entry each edition.
stories.wy: Client-driven requirement (REQ-2026-036, raised by Elena Potapov for ANWR) — brands like BMW/MINI/Rolls-Royce are long-term assets that outlive seasonal products, and losing them each edition undermines the platform's reuse value for recurring, brand-driven events.
stories.oc: Exhibitor Import (both new-to-event and update cases) and "add from Global Database" now auto-attach an exhibitor's existing brands, and their product/category relations where matches exist, to the target event, with no template or UI change required.
stories.pae: component Admin Interface; exhibitor import carrying brands → Data Import

stories.s: Adds a nested Region sub-filter under Country (web only) so visitors can narrow exhibitor/participant listings by region, not just by country.
stories.pr: The Country filter was flat, with no way to narrow results to a region within a country, even on events where Region is captured on the registration form.
stories.wy: Requested by organizers, mirroring the existing nested Activity/Interest category filter pattern.
stories.oc: A new optional (default-off) Regions sub-filter nested under Country across Exhibitors/Pavilions/Brands/Products and Delegates/Speakers/Buyers admin tabs; web-only, with mobile explicitly unaffected.
stories.pae: components Admin Interface + Profile map to two products; region sub-filter under Country for exhibitor/participant listings; chose Profile (the country/region profile data), Admin / Platform Core equally plausible

stories.s: Polishes Global Search's results page (persistent search field, clearer counts, equal-size News cards, relabeled sponsor blocks) based on direct IMEX customer feedback.
stories.pr: Users at IMEX flagged friction points in the newly released Global Search results page: a closable search field that could disappear, confusingly placed result counts, an oversized first News card, and unclear sponsored labels.
stories.wy: Direct field feedback from a major trade show (IMEX) following the initial Global Search launch (EP-47675).
stories.oc: The search field is now permanently visible below the sponsored banner; result counts moved onto "Show all" buttons with a summed page-level total; News cards are now equal-sized in a single scroll row; "Sponsors" relabeled "Sponsored Exhibitors"/"Sponsored Products".

stories.s: Onboarding/research task building developer fluency in Ticketing and a proposed new architecture (PR #4510) ahead of a planned Ticketing refactor.
stories.pr: No production changes; the team needs a developer fluent in both how Ticketing currently works end-to-end (admin setup, purchase, upgrades) and the new architectural pattern proposed in PR #4510, before any refactor of the current monolith code can begin.
stories.wy: Prerequisite knowledge-building step for a planned future Ticketing refactor.
stories.oc: Developer understanding of Ticketing end-to-end and the new architecture pattern from PR #4510, plus a documented list of candidate refactor areas; no code changes.

stories.s: Fixes IconModal's padding, gaps and title typography to match the Figma design system exactly, removing per-consumer style patches across ~41 call sites.
stories.pr: IconModal's theme styling had drifted from the Figma spec (wrong title size/line-height, wrong close-button offset, inconsistent padding/gap composition, missing border, wrong default width), affecting roughly 41 call sites in admin-ui plus shared library consumers, each patched locally instead of fixed at the root.
stories.wy: Design-system-fidelity issue surfaced by comparing the shipped component against its Figma spec node; the current "correct" spacing only worked by coincidence, not by design.
stories.oc: Reworked slot styles (uniform 24px padding, single 32px gap, correct 18px/1.2 bold title, 8px radius plus border, 424px default width), full Storybook coverage of slot combinations, and removal of local sx/width workarounds in admin-ui.
stories.pae: design-system IconModal fix

stories.s: Closes a bypass where direct URL navigation let restricted users open the add/edit product form even when the UI correctly hid the button.
stories.pr: The "can add/edit a product" gating logic lived only in the Add button's UI state; navigating directly to /profile/products?add=true (or ?edit=<id>) bypassed every disabling condition (limit reached, disabled products, relogin member), letting restricted users open and submit the product form anyway.
stories.wy: Security/business-logic gap discovered in review; needed to prevent users from exceeding configured product limits or editing restrictions via URL manipulation.
stories.oc: Routing decisions now use the same single "can add/can edit" gate as the button; unauthorized direct navigation redirects to the product list instead of rendering the form, with backend enforcement also to be verified.
stories.pae: summary: profile products add/edit form guard → Product Form

stories.s: Scoping spike estimating the effort, risks and infrastructure needed to migrate the Exhibitors search engine to AI Search.
stories.pr: Before implementing the switch to AI Search (EP-55996), the team lacks a clear technical picture of the effort, risks and infrastructure requirements involved.
stories.wy: Needed so the team can estimate EP-55996 confidently and the EM can plan the work into a sprint.
stories.oc: A technical brief (target state, gap analysis, risks/open questions, phased plan with T-shirt estimates) published and linked to EP-55996.
stories.pae: epic 'Switch AI Search for Marketplace' → Search and Filters

stories.s: Extends Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments search to match Account ID, so client ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East can cross-check transactions against Stripe quickly.
stories.pr: Search on the Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages covered name/surname/email but explicitly excluded Account ID, so the client (ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East) couldn't quickly cross-reference a transaction against their Stripe account/customer reference without scrolling paginated results.
stories.wy: Direct client request and follow-on from the earlier search feature (EP-54690), confirmed feasible by engineering.
stories.oc: The existing search field/button on both pages now also matches (partial) Account ID / ID, with the same trigger, reset and empty-state behavior as the original name/email search.
stories.pae: component Payments; Account ID search on Transaction Dashboard

stories.s: Fixes product upload endpoints so slow file I/O no longer blocks the DB transaction and concurrent uploads can no longer silently overwrite each other's result.
stories.pr: Product upload endpoints ran slow external file I/O (up to ~10s) inside a database transaction, holding pooled connections under load, and two concurrent uploads or an upload racing a delete/update on the same product could silently overwrite each other's result, leaving an orphaned file in storage forever.
stories.wy: Correctness and scalability defect discovered in the product upload path; needed before it causes data loss or connection exhaustion at scale.
stories.oc: Uploads now validate and store the file first with no open transaction, then link it in a short transaction with permission/limit checks re-run; failed links auto-clean the stored file; concurrent writes to the same product now queue via row locking instead of silently overwriting; ~30 new unit tests, API contract unchanged.
stories.pae: component Open API (not in table); epic 'Migration of endpoints (Public API v3)' → product upload endpoints

stories.s: Fixes a caching bug where cookie-dependent/signed-in pages were marked publicly cacheable, risking one visitor's personalized page being served to another.
stories.pr: Every route, including signed-in and cookie-dependent pages, returned Cache-Control: public with no Vary: Cookie, so a shared CDN could serve one user's cached response (e.g. a signup redirect decision) to a different visitor.
stories.wy: DevOps enabled CDN caching for custom domains and asked the frontend team to confirm cookie-dependent pages weren't marked public before extending caching further.
stories.oc: Routes split into anonymous (kept public/cacheable) vs personal (private, no-store) groups; Vary: Cookie added where relevant; audited that no public response carries Set-Cookie; a route/header matrix handed to DevOps.
stories.pae: Cache-Control header bug across all routes; platform infrastructure

stories.s: Addresses remaining Global Search backend code-review findings: constructor-based config, policy-layer access checks, and hardened error handling.
stories.pr: Global Search's backend carries deferred code-review findings: brittle setter-based configuration, a duplicated access-control rule sitting outside the policy layer, catch-all exception handling, and DS failures silently reported as flags instead of raised as exceptions.
stories.wy: Agreed follow-up from the EP-47675 Global Search code review.
stories.oc: Constructor-based configuration, access rule moved into a policy, hardened typing and exception handling, followed by a review/QA pass.
stories.pae: v2 search consistency: search infrastructure with no user-facing surface — [TechDebt] Global Search backend refactoring from code review; no product component

stories.s: Rebuilds Switch to use theme color variants (mirroring Radio/Checkbox), deleting the custom Switch component in favor of a themed MUI Switch.
stories.pr: Switch was a custom component that defined its primary color directly in root styles instead of via theme color variants, unlike the already-unified Radio and Checkbox.
stories.wy: Consistency follow-up to the Radio (EP-55105) and Checkbox (EP-55397) unification work.
stories.oc: Switch colors implemented via theme variants; the custom Switch component deleted; usages replaced with FormControlLabel plus MUI Switch and slotProps; Storybook updated. Cross-repo consumer migration is separate follow-up work.
stories.pae: design-system Switch normalisation

stories.s: Rebuilds Tag, StatusTag, Track, FilterChip and Badge as one theme-integrated Chip family so any app can restyle them via the MUI theme, additive to existing components.
stories.pr: Tag and StatusTag were built with ad-hoc sx functions and a string-keyed style lookup, not wired into the MUI theme, so consuming apps could only override them via sx/className, not theme.components.
stories.wy: Design review found that 5 seemingly different Figma specs (Tags, Status tags, Tracks, Filter chips, Badges) are actually variations of one MUI Chip primitive; agreed via a documented ADR process.
stories.oc: A new chips/ category with 5 theme-registered components (Tag, StatusTag, Track, FilterChip, Badge) ships additively, alongside the untouched originals; cross-repo migration in admin-ui/portal-ui is scoped as follow-up work.
stories.pae: design-system Chip family rebuild

stories.s: Adds force and dry-run flags to manual AutoUpdate sync triggers, unblocking HubSpot Push-Back and future push-back integrations.
stories.pr: Manual AutoUpdate sync triggers had no way to bypass change-suppression gates (to force mapping changes through) or preview what a run would do without writing, a capability HubSpot Push-Back and future integrations like Cvent need.
stories.wy: Direct blocker for EP-55471 (HubSpot Push-Back); benefits all future push-back integrations.
stories.oc: force and dryRun flags threaded from the manual trigger through SyncJob to per-entity queue payloads; force bypasses both push- and pull-side suppression gates; dryRun logs WOULD_PUSH/WOULD_SKIP verdicts with no writes on the push side (rejected on the pull side); scheduled runs are unaffected; metrics track dry-run outcomes separately.
stories.pae: component Native Integration (not in table); AutoUpdate sync force/dry-run flags → Integration HUB

stories.s: Adds Paid amount and Payment status columns, plus a paid-only filter, to the registrant custom report, ending manual cross-referencing against the separate Payments report.
stories.pr: Payment data and registrant form data lived in two disconnected report systems, joined only through a multi-hop Registration to Account to Event to Participant to Order to Payment chain, so organizers had no single accurate view of who had actually paid.
stories.wy: Organizer need for an accurate paid-registrant list without manual cross-referencing between two separate reports.
stories.oc: "Paid amount" and "Payment status" (friendly labels: Paid/Pending/Failed/Cancelled/No payment record) added as selectable Visitor custom-report columns, plus a "Paid only" filter; registrants with no linked order are shown, not silently dropped.
stories.pae: component Reporting; registrant report paid columns → Exportable Reports (Online Registration §4.14 reports also relevant)

stories.s: Extracts Saved Search Queries logic from the controller into a proper service/repository layer, fixing a replica-lag eviction bug by construction.
stories.pr: SearchSuggestionsController inlined the same account/event scope, a 20-entry cap rule, ad-hoc request parsing and a copy-pasted access gate across three actions, making the cap rule untestable without HTTP and vulnerable to a read-replica-lag bug on cap eviction.
stories.wy: Agreed structural follow-up from the EP-55336 code review, modeled on the existing Favourite service layer (EP-53978).
stories.oc: New SavedQueryService plus read/write repositories (write operations forced onto the master connection), a request validation object, a response resource, domain exceptions, a feature-toggle module gate, a README, and unit tests for the cap/eviction rule; the controller becomes thin delegates and the existing 13-test behavioural suite stays green.
stories.pae: v2 search consistency: search infrastructure with no user-facing surface — Saved Search Queries controller → service-layer refactor (tech debt); no product component

stories.s: Stops mobile Schedule, Speaker Profile and Exhibitor Profile pages from showing empty image placeholders, matching the fix already applied to the Sessions list.
stories.pr: The global "Display Image Placeholders" setting forced a large empty placeholder on Schedule, Speaker Profile and Exhibitor Profile pages whenever no logo/image was uploaded, and unlike web there's no CSS workaround available on the mobile app.
stories.wy: Brings these three surfaces in line with the Sessions list's existing logo-or-nothing behavior, which mobile organizers otherwise have no way to manage.
stories.oc: Schedule (both sessions and exhibitor events), Speaker Profile (session logos) and Exhibitor Profile (exhibitor-event images) now show nothing rather than a placeholder when no image is uploaded; every other list governed by the setting is unaffected; mobile only.
stories.pae: component Mobile App; schedule/profile placeholder images

stories.s: Moves the Cloning module onto the standard module bootstrap and turns on automated architecture-boundary checks, unblocking the rest of its modernization.
stories.pr: Cloning is the only src/ module still on the legacy bootstrap path that once took the whole application down when it shipped without src/ present, and with no boundary-check gate, architecture conformance rests entirely on manual review, which two independent review passes already proved unreliable.
stories.wy: Prerequisite for all later Cloning modernization stages (transaction-runner swap, dependency-direction cleanup); establishes the violation-count baseline that later stages burn down.
stories.oc: CloningModuleProvider replaces the legacy DI.php registration; new deptrac layer blocks (in warning mode) enumerate architecture violations; a CI pipeline step runs deptrac; a provider-resolution test guards every registered service; a live clone still runs end to end.
stories.pae: epic '[CLONING] New Modules Architecture conformance' → Event Cloning; module bootstrap

stories.s: Fixes the Cloning module's inverted dependencies so its core logic can be unit tested without a database and can't be silently broken by internal renames.
stories.pr: Cloning's Application and Domain layers depend directly on Infrastructure (and even on each other in the wrong direction), so basic logic can't be tested without Postgres, a viewer-permission decision leaked into a Domain value object, and CLI workers reference internal classes directly.
stories.wy: Directly answers an external team's code review finding that dependencies must point inward and currently do not; the violations are specific and enumerated.
stories.oc: Contract DTOs introduced so Domain stops importing Contract; Application now depends only on ports; use-case classes moved into Application without dragging Infrastructure along; a thin CLI presentation layer added; the internal service-locator pattern removed; the contract split into read vs command halves, with deptrac reporting zero Domain/Application violations at completion.
stories.pae: epic '[CLONING] New Modules Architecture conformance' → Event Cloning; layer boundaries

stories.s: Documents the SharedKernel/Platform architecture rules (previously only in config comments) and fixes stale namespace references, to prevent repeat incidents like EP-55938.
stories.pr: The rules for where cross-cutting code belongs (SharedKernel vs Platform vs a new module) live only inside deptrac config comments with no README, and this already caused a real incident (EP-55938) where shared Alerting code was wrongly placed as its own module and had to be relocated; three existing READMEs also teach a namespace (Modules\\SharedKernel) that doesn't exist.
stories.wy: Surfaced from the Cloning module work but applies platform-wide; can run in parallel with Stage 0 and blocks nobody.
stories.oc: New README.md files for src/SharedKernel and src/Platform explaining what belongs where and the "cross-cutting is never a new module" rule (citing EP-55938 as the worked example); stale namespace references fixed in three existing READMEs; the outside-import axis and rule-document location gaps documented.
stories.pae: [TechDept] documentation of SharedKernel / framework rules; serves no single product

stories.s: Fixes the admin chatbot's RAG endpoint to be configurable per environment at runtime, preventing production admin traffic from silently hitting the dev AI service.
stories.pr: The Expo Assistant chatbot's RAG endpoint was effectively hardcoded to the dev Generation Service at build time with no working per-environment override; different Docker setups either lost the chatbot entirely (EKS) or baked in the dev URL, so production risked silently sending real admin oauth tokens to a dev-tier service with no in-app signal.
stories.wy: Needed correct, safe per-environment chatbot configuration before wider environment rollout.
stories.oc: generate-config.js now emits the RAG endpoint into runtime config.js, regenerated on container start with no SPA rebuild needed; DevOps injects the variable per environment; verified across all four resolution paths. The equivalent problem in the legacy monolith admin is explicitly out of scope, tracked separately.
stories.pae: admin chatbot RAG endpoint environment config; no documented feature

stories.s: Onboarding and impact-assessment spike scoping how much of Hyve's Flexible Generation Settings the existing Speed Networking service already supports.
stories.pr: A newly assigned engineer needs working knowledge of the speed-networking-service codebase and matching algorithm before Flexible Generation Settings (HV-265) can be accurately scoped into implementation.
stories.wy: Needed before the Flexible Generation Settings requirements can be scoped and estimated against the current service.
stories.oc: A requirement-by-requirement assessment of what's already supported, partially supported, or net-new work for Flexible Generation Settings.
stories.pae: epic 'Meeting program. Flexible generation settings' → Meeting Program; Speed Networking service assessment

stories.s: Flags that opted-out users' favourites stay permanently private while their views/downloads/scans reappear on re-opt-in, and asks product to choose one consistent privacy model.
stories.pr: Favourites are protected on the write side (the event is never emitted for opted-out users, so the data never exists), while views, downloads and scans are protected only on the read side (the data is written but masked at query time), so opting back in retroactively un-hides a user's entire opted-out interaction history except favourites, and the read-side mask depends on a consent dictionary that's ~48% incomplete.
stories.wy: Two separate engineering fixes (favourites vs. the rest) created a visible asymmetry that needs a single product ruling rather than another point fix.
stories.oc: Three concrete options laid out (permanent write-side private tracking for everything, keep read-side masking as the standard, or split by signal strength) with measured costs and trade-offs for each, so the product team can make and record a decision.
stories.pae: summary: opted-out privacy for favourites vs passive interactions → Favourites/interactions privacy; cross-cutting data privacy equally plausible

stories.s: Fixes the OpenAPI doc generator to report real failures instead of always exiting 0, after a swallowed error already caused a spec-drift bug to be misdiagnosed.
stories.pr: composer docs always exits 0 regardless of failure, because the dispatcher discards exec() exit codes and each of the five doc generators swallows its own exceptions, so a stale, never-regenerated OpenAPI spec is indistinguishable from a fresh one.
stories.wy: Root-cause fix for a documented false-diagnosis incident (EP-56062, where three test cases were wrongly marked BLOCKED because nobody could tell if the served spec reflected the code).
stories.oc: The dispatcher now uses passthru() and stops at the first non-zero exit; all five generators write failures to STDERR and exit(1); behavior verified against real success and failure cases.
stories.pae: OpenAPI doc generator exit codes; build tooling

stories.s: Mutation-tests the Cloning pipeline's stuck-task monitor on dev/alpha, then schedules it across all production environments.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.wy: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.pae: summary: [CLONING] stuck-task monitor → Event Cloning

stories.s: Triages and fixes 7 long-failing frontend test suites (39 tests) and 23 type-check errors so CI can gate on a clean green/red signal again.
stories.pr: 7 pre-existing failing test suites (39 tests) predate a recent unrelated change and mask any new regression in those suites, forcing every review to be gated against a stale "known failures" baseline instead of a clean green/red check, plus 23 pre-existing type-check errors in 2 test files.
stories.wy: Restores CI/test trustworthiness so a real regression inside these suites can no longer hide.
stories.oc: All 7 suites triaged (stale test vs. real defect) and fixed, 23 type-check errors eliminated, and the full suite is green (0 failed of 1599 tests).
stories.pae: fix failing frontend tests; test infrastructure

stories.s: Replaces VISIT's uncontrollable webhook resync (which could flood the queue) with guarded, observable AutoUpdate polling and a configurable near-real-time sync interval.
stories.pr: VISIT sync was an opaque black box — resync deleted and recreated the webhook from scratch with no lock, no progress visibility and no history, so repeated manual resync clicks stacked concurrent replays that flooded the processing queue until the integration stopped responding.
stories.wy: Needed to make VISIT sync observable, guardable and safe to retry, replacing an architecture that could self-inflict a denial-of-service.
stories.oc: VISIT visitor/exhibitor sync migrated to AutoUpdate's revision-based polling (guarded against overlapping runs, visible in sync history); webhooks removed entirely; a new configurable per-subscription polling interval (VISIT gets 1 minute vs. the 5-minute default) preserves VISIT's near-instant feel; profile-picture push-back migrated to its own AutoUpdate subscription.
stories.pae: component Native Integration (not in table); epic 'Native Integrations - Migrations' → Integration HUB (VISIT sync)

stories.s: Enforces braces on every control statement via ESLint, closing the gap between the documented code convention and what CI actually checks.
stories.pr: The FRON code conventions require braces on every if/else/for/while, but the inherited ESLint config only requires braces for multi-line bodies, so ~30 braceless statements exist and every new one has to be caught manually — the classic place where adding a second statement silently changes control flow.
stories.wy: Closes the gap between the documented convention and what CI actually enforces.
stories.oc: .eslintrc now sets curly: ["error", "all"]; ~30 existing braceless occurrences auto-fixed; test suite and type-check baseline confirmed unchanged.
stories.pae: ESLint rule; code convention

stories.s: Renamed 18 inconsistently-named constants files and removed a dead re-export shim so engineers stop copying the wrong naming convention.
stories.pr: Two inconsistent naming spellings for constants files (72 vs 18) caused convention drift, and a redundant root re-export shim added unnecessary indirection.
stories.wy: Found during a frontend code-conventions audit; a cheap fix that stops new files from copying the wrong pattern and keeps the documented convention true to the tree.
stories.oc: 18 files renamed to the standard *.constants.ts spelling, ~106-132 import sites updated, the dead systemPages re-export shim removed with its 24 importers repointed, and one unused file deleted.
stories.pae: file renaming; code convention

stories.s: Fixed a timing bug so meeting-program and speed-networking timelines update live at the true start instead of only at the next segment's end, plus hardened animation and accessibility.
stories.pr: Users viewing the meeting-program/speed-networking timeline before it started would not see it update (e.g. the "Requests" block) at the actual start time - only when the first segment ended or the page reloaded.
stories.wy: Discovered while fixing a related portal-ui bug (HV-419); the shared hook is reused elsewhere, so a workaround wasn't sufficient and a root-cause fix was warranted.
stories.oc: useTimeline now wakes exactly at the segment start, self-heals from index gaps/duplicates, re-arms for waits over 24h, and the progress-bar animation moved to performant CSS transitions; added accessibility roles and 23 tests across the component.
stories.pae: summary: Timeline component for meeting-program and speed-networking timelines → Meeting Program

stories.s: Authored the cross-team RFC defining how the meeting-generation algorithm will support organizer-configurable pair priorities and per-run settings, unblocking the next two build phases.
stories.pr: The current meeting-generation algorithm has a rigid, implicit priority model (sponsored/free-from-sponsored/free) that doesn't match new requirements for organizer-configurable pair ordering and per-run eligibility rules; the design needed cross-team sign-off (DS, Hyve backend, Hyve frontend) before implementation could be scoped.
stories.wy: Direct follow-on to the approved onboarding/impact-assessment spike (EP-56106); needed to settle open design questions and de-risk the two follow-up implementation tasks (pair-queue rework, per-run settings) before they could be estimated.
stories.oc: An RFC was authored and readied covering the organizer-ordered pair-queue/priority model, per-run eligibility toggles (relevance requirement, shared team relevance, ignore blocked timeslots), open questions (e.g. "prioritise role" scope, a default-value mismatch), and rollout sequencing; no implementation shipped, per the ticket's explicit scope.
stories.pae: component Speed Networking (not in table); epic 'Meeting program. Flexible generation settings' → Meeting Program

stories.s: Fixed the root cause of recurring flaky CI test failures and updated the QA agent's own standards so it stops generating the same class of async-assertion bug.
stories.pr: Unit tests failed randomly across parallel CI shards, blocking merges and eroding trust in build results ("developers learn to ignore red builds") - a recurrence of two earlier tickets whose fixes addressed only one mechanism, not the general class of bug.
stories.wy: Merge-blocking pipeline instability directly costs engineering time, and the recurrence pattern meant the underlying test-writing standard needed to change, not just receive another one-off patch.
stories.oc: Fixed at root cause by asserting on the actually-awaited async content instead of using loader-disappearance as a proxy; added an explicit async-assertion rule to the QA agent's skill doc and a repeated-run determinism check to its workflow so future generated tests can't reintroduce the same flake class.
stories.pae: flaky CI tests; test infrastructure

stories.s: Registered 8 out-of-convention Redux store domains into the shared barrel so all store selectors and actions are reachable through one consistent import path.
stories.pr: Eight newer Redux domains skipped the required barrel-export registration, so imports were split between a documented "public API" barrel and inconsistent deep imports, undermining the convention's reliability.
stories.wy: Found during a phase-4 conventions audit (EP-56258); the drift compounds every time a new slice is scaffolded following the correct barrel pattern, widening the inconsistency further.
stories.oc: Added index.ts barrels for the 8 domains and registered them in the central store barrel, resolving symbol-name collisions, without a disruptive bulk rewrite of existing deep imports.
stories.pae: Redux store barrel; code convention

stories.pr: Test cases inherited from teststone were almost all mis-classified as expensive end-to-end tests rather than placed at the cheapest layer that actually verifies the behaviour, and pointed at frozen teststone branches that won't exist once teststone is archived.
stories.wy: Required step in the broader migration off teststone (to Codeception/Pest + e2e-testing); needed before the 9 linked product V3 tickets' tests could be trusted as the real regression suite.
stories.oc: All 188 test cases re-leveled per the "lowest sufficient level" rule with justifications recorded, repointed to their real implementation repos, stale/mismatched cases corrected, and coverage gaps made explicit rather than silently over-claimed.
stories.pae: component Open API (not in table); epic 'Migrate Integration-team tests…' → test-level re-levelling of product V3 test catalogue; test coverage (Integrations Public API v3 is the subject)

stories.s: Catalogued all API endpoints used for Exhibitor CRUD to ground the upcoming Exhibitor CRUD module build.
stories.pr: Before building or refactoring exhibitor CRUD functionality, the team lacked a documented inventory of which endpoints perform create, read, update and delete on exhibitors.
stories.wy: Necessary discovery step to de-risk and scope the "Implement Exhibitor CRUD" epic.
stories.oc: A list of Exhibitor CRUD endpoints annotated by action type (Create/Read/Update/Delete) was produced.

stories.wy: Committed to on a 7 Aug team call as a prerequisite before any ExpoIntelligence story could be properly estimated or started.
stories.oc: A findings report classifying each of the 22 metrics as Have/Partial/Missing with rough effort signals, cross-checked against the DP2.0 Parity Matrix; no dashboards or queries were built, per the ticket's explicit scope.

stories.s: Removed a slow full-team prefetch that delayed opening Bulk Respond for large exhibitor teams, replacing it with an instant open and a simple post-apply data refresh.
stories.pr: Opening Bulk Respond on any exhibitor team with more than 60 pending meeting-relevance assignments triggered a multi-request sequential prefetch before the button was even clickable, solely to build a client-side patch that was never rendered.
stories.wy: The prefetch (and a second hidden sweep) existed only to support an optimistic client-side patch; removing them entirely, rather than swapping the data source, eliminated both the delay and a data-correctness risk in the patch logic.
stories.oc: Bulk Respond now opens instantly regardless of team size; after a successful bulk action, only the current grid page is refetched fresh from the backend and every other cached page is invalidated.
stories.pae: summary: Bulk Respond for exhibitor team pending meeting assignments → Meeting Confirmation/Cancellation

stories.s: Migrated the Media module's public contract from internal value objects to plain primitives, keeping it aligned with the platform's modular, extraction-ready architecture.
stories.pr: The Media module's Contract layer still used SharedKernel value objects (ImageId, MediaId, id collections) in its public signatures, contradicting the newly-adopted convention that Contract surfaces must stay primitive and dependency-free so modules can eventually be extracted independently.
stories.wy: New-monolith architecture convention adopted in EP-52842; the Media module predated it and needed to catch up, the same as Categories/Locations/Exhibition already had.
stories.oc: Media module Contract signatures now use primitives (int, int[], ?int); VO translation moved into facade implementations; consuming code (mainly the Product module) updated accordingly.
stories.pae: Media module contract refactor; architecture

stories.pr: Only the "My Account" and "Event Info" screens used the new Gabarito font; the remaining ~451 layouts (about 1010 text elements) were left on inconsistent default fonts, breaking the intended unified look end to end.
stories.wy: Client/brand-consistency requirement for the FBM app; a PO note flagging residual visual risk indicates this shipped ahead of an event under time pressure.
stories.oc: Gabarito Semibold/Light configured platform-wide for FBM in AppBuilder; ~252 components (AppCompatTextView, TextView, MaterialButton, chips, radio buttons, text inputs) migrated onto the dynamic-font path; verified with no truncation/overflow on a smoke-tested set of high-traffic screens.
